__readme: Shared parity fixtures for ExecutionBudgets — the eval/swarm clock contract. Loaded by sdk/tests/contract/execution-budgets.test.ts in mcpjam-inspector (the canonical implementation, sdk/src/contract/execution-budgets.ts) AND, VERBATIM, by tests/convex/executionBudgetsParity.test.ts in mcpjam-backend (the hand-mirrored table + resolver in convex/lib/executionBudgets.ts). The backend cannot import @mcpjam/sdk into convex/ default-runtime code, so this file is the only common ground truth — copy it byte for byte, do not re-author it, and register it in convex/lib/mirrors.json. LOAD RULE: strip EVERY key whose name starts with '__' before handing a row to a validator or resolver; they are fixture annotations (__label, __why) and the authored schemas are .strict(). MILLISECONDS EVERYWHERE — minutes exist only in rendering, so every number below is ms. The 'table' block pins the platform defaults and ceilings (§3.2): if an assertion there fails, the two tables have drifted and a run would get different clocks depending on which side resolved it — STOP, do not edit one side to match the other without changing both. The 'resolve' cases each name an 'args' (authored budgets, plus the surface whose defaults/ceilings column to use, plus an optional org ceiling override) and an 'expect' that is either a full resolved object with per-field sources, or a violations list. 'ceilingOverride' cases pin the LOWER-ONLY rule: effective = min(platform, org) — and, in the 'resolve' block, that the effective ceiling caps a DEFAULTED field too, so an org ceiling below a platform default is not sailed over by a suite that authored nothing. Capping applies to the default rung only: an authored value above the ceiling is still REFUSED, never capped. When the contract shape changes, edit BOTH implementations AND this fixture in the same PR.

table.__label: Platform defaults and ceilings, per surface (§3.2)

resolve.__label: evals — nothing authored: the defaults column, every source 'default'
resolve.__why: This is the path a run launched before budgets were ever written takes. It must be byte-identical to the platform table, so no runner needs a legacy branch.

resolve.__label: swarms — nothing authored: the swarm defaults, which differ from evals
resolve.__why: toolCallTimeoutMs (120s vs 30s), unitTimeoutMs (20min vs 10min) and runTimeoutMs (2h vs 30min) are surface-specific. A mirror that collapsed the two columns would pass every eval case and still be wrong.

resolve.__label: evals — every field authored within the ceiling: authored wins, every source 'authored'
evals — partial authoring mixes sources per field
resolve.__why: Provenance is per FIELD, not per object: a suite that set only its iteration clock must still record that the other four came from the platform.

resolve.__label: swarms — sessionTimeoutMs feeds the same unitTimeoutMs slot
resolve.__why: 'unit' exists only on the resolved shape. Authors write the word that means something on their surface; every runtime consumer reads one field name.

resolve.__label: evals — above the platform ceiling is REFUSED, not clamped, and names the authored spelling
resolve.__why: A run must never execute with a different number from the one its author wrote. The violation says 'iterationTimeoutMs' because that is the word in the suite — telling someone their 'unitTimeoutMs' is too large names a field they have never seen.

resolve.__label: org ceiling LOWERS the platform ceiling, and refuses what used to fit
resolve.__why: effective = min(platform, org). 30 min is well under the 2h platform ceiling, so this exact suite resolves fine without the override and is refused with it.

resolve.__label: an org ceiling BELOW the platform default caps the default too
resolve.__why: The swarm run default is 2h and the platform ceiling 12h, so an org that caps runs at 1h is asking for something no authored value even mentions. Copying the default past it would let every unauthored suite in that org sail over the cap — a ceiling an unauthored run ignores is not a ceiling. This is not the clamping the contract forbids: that rule protects a number a person wrote, and nobody wrote this one, so the source stays 'default'.

resolve.__label: an authored value still wins over a default the ceiling capped
resolve.__why: Capping applies to the DEFAULT rung only. An authored value at or under the effective ceiling is used as written, and one above it is still refused rather than capped.

resolve.__label: org ceiling can never RAISE a platform ceiling
resolve.__why: An org column naming 24h against a 12h platform run ceiling is ignored for that field: raising is not expressible in v1, and a plan-tiered LIMIT_NAME is a pricing-page change, deliberately deferred.

resolve.__label: a value exactly ON the ceiling is allowed
resolve.__why: The comparison is strictly greater-than. An off-by-one here silently refuses the largest legal suite in the product.

Zero is the one value a truthiness check would read as 'unset' and silently replace with the default 2 — which is the whole bug this contract exists to end: a retry policy that is an accident rather than a decision.

ceilingOverride.__label: no override returns the platform column unchanged
a partial override lowers only the fields it names
an override above the platform ceiling is ignored for that field

authoredSchema.__label: Rows the AUTHORED zod schemas must accept or reject, before any ceiling is consulted
authoredSchema.__why: Each authored bound's max IS the platform ceiling, so parsing alone refuses what the platform could never run; the resolver's check is what catches an org ceiling that lowered it. '.strict()' is what stops 'iterationTimeoutMs' being accepted on a swarm, which would otherwise resolve to the swarm default and silently ignore the author.

accept.__label: evals — minimum legal values on every field
swarms — minimum legal values on every field

reject.__label: evals — sessionTimeoutMs is not an eval word
swarms — iterationTimeoutMs is not a swarm word
unitTimeoutMs is never authorable on either surface
below the floor — a 1s turn budget is a misconfiguration, not a tight one
above the platform ceiling is refused by parsing alone
